questions.q: What distinguishes Application Insights from Metrics Explorer and Log Analytics?
options: It replaces the need for a Log Analytics workspace entirely
It only works with .NET applications
It only collects data once a day
It auto-instruments application code to produce requests, dependencies, and exceptions automatically
questions.explain: Application Insights is Azure Monitor's APM layer — once attached, it auto-instruments the application to capture requests, dependency calls, and exceptions without custom telemetry code.

questions.q: On the Application Map, what does a node turning red typically indicate?
options: The component is unhealthy — e.g., failing calls or high latency
The node is receiving zero traffic
The node's billing has reached its budget
The node has been deleted
questions.explain: The Application Map colors each node by health based on its telemetry. A red node signals failures or degraded performance in that component, often before anyone notices through other means.

questions.q: What do you see when you drill from an Application Map node into 'end-to-end transaction details'?
options: The resource's deployment history
The full timeline of every hop one specific request made across the system
A list of all users currently online
A billing summary for that resource
questions.explain: End-to-end transaction details show one request's complete path hop by hop, with the duration of each hop — Azure's equivalent of a distributed trace.

questions.q: When would you reach for Live Metrics instead of the Application Map or Log Analytics?
options: When you want to watch telemetry unfold in near real time, such as during a deployment
When you need to edit application source code
When you need data older than 90 days
When you want to delete telemetry data
questions.explain: Live Metrics streams telemetry with about one second of latency, filterable on the fly — ideal for watching something happen live, like a canary rollout, rather than querying data that's already landed.

questions.q: What is 'auto-instrumentation' in the context of Application Insights?
options: An alert type that fires automatically
A manual process requiring a custom logging statement for every call
A feature that only works for exceptions, not requests
Telemetry automatically collected once Application Insights is attached, with no custom code required
questions.explain: Auto-instrumentation means Application Insights captures requests, dependencies, and exceptions automatically once it's wired into the app — no hand-written telemetry needed for each call.
